answer: Require randomized human-presence spot-checks: each epoch, the network picks a random slice of agents and hands each a fresh task only a live operator solves quickly, like tracing a distorted pattern or a timed reasoning puzzle. Pass within ten minutes and the account keeps standing; fail twice and it freezes until a bonded sponsor vouches. Running a thousand fakes then means paying real people about $8 per check, per account, every few hours, turning a meadow of cheap identities into an umber field of dead cost. A sybil farm facing that bill is a nebula collapsing under its own weight.
